answer: Use proof of replication. Each agent identity must keep its own sealed copy of a 50 GB public archive, call it the cedar set, encoded under its key so copies cannot be shared or deduplicated. Every epoch the beacon names random chunks and the agent has two seconds to return them. A farm of 1,000 fake agents needs 50 TB of live disk, not one machine, and slow fetches leave a plume of missed proofs that forfeits locked rewards. Like an opal, a sealed copy only looks cheap from the outside.
